content.comment_body: The [article_no] manual states that this device can only save up to 2000 records per datalog file on the SD card. Why is there such a limitation? I would expect an 8GB SD card to store much more data.

You are correct; the maximum number of datalog entries per file is 2000 for this hardware, and this cannot be modified. However, if you perform a RUN/STOP cycle, a new datalog file will be generated on the SD card. Using the software, only the most recent datalog file can be accessed; to read older files, you need to use a card reader. The remaining space on the SD card can still be used for other data, such as documentation or service packs.

Although the restriction may seem problematic, it is sufficient in most real-world cases. There are alternative approaches available, and ultimately, it’s important to evaluate how these data management options align with your project needs.
The maximum number of entries is set at 2000, and this cannot be changed. Regards, [url]

analysis.insight_summary: Users highlight the hard limit of 2000 datalog records per file imposed by the hardware, which is independent of the actual SD card storage size. This hardware-based cap requires users to organize their data collection within the specified restriction, though other file types can still be stored on the SD card.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect to utilize the full storage capability of large SD cards for logging, and wish to store more than 2000 records per file to maximize their SD card usage.
